papers_read.title_as_printed: An end-to-end multimodal 3D CNN framework with multi-level features for the prediction of mild cognitive impairment (Zhang et al., Knowledge-Based Systems 281 (2023) 111064)
Class activation attention transfer neural networks for MCI conversion prediction (Luo et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 156 (2023) 106700)

what_each_reports.P-72: Twin 3D ResNet18 with attention, multi-level features and spatial pyramid pooling on ADNI baseline sMRI grey matter plus FDG-PET (850 subjects). The 94.61% is AD vs NC accuracy (215 AD/246 NC). On MCI conversion (sMCI vs pMCI, conversion within 3 years; 238 sMCI/151 pMCI) the multimodal model reports 77.19% accuracy (AUC 0.755; five-fold on a fixed subset 77.19 +/- 1.24); the sMRI-only MAResNet18 reports 73.68% (AUC 0.721). Subject-level 70/15/15 split, averaged over three test subsets.
what_each_reports.P-3: Class Activation Attention Transfer 3D CNN ensemble on baseline T1 MRI only, ADNI1/2, 298 sMCI/295 pMCI (conversion within 36 months), Wen et al. benchmark splits, 5-fold CV: pMCI vs sMCI accuracy 74.61% (variance 0.002), AUC 0.780, sensitivity/specificity 0.75/0.75.

quantity_a: As claimed: AD vs NC accuracy from sMRI+FDG-PET (94.61%). P-72's own T2 quantity: sMCI vs pMCI (3-year) accuracy from sMRI+FDG-PET (77.19%) or sMRI alone (73.68%), ADNI, subject-level hold-out
quantity_b: sMCI vs pMCI (36-month) accuracy from baseline T1 MRI only, ADNI1/2 (593 subjects), 5-fold CV on Wen et al. splits
incompatible_if_same: No. The claimed 94.61% is not a T2 result. Comparing like with like, P-72's MRI-only conversion accuracy (73.68%) and P-3's (74.61%) are within one point, and P-72's multimodal 77.19% is about 2.6 points above P-3 with a test set of roughly 57 MCI subjects per split, so the intervals overlap. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch as claimed (P-72's 94.61% is AD vs NC, not T2); match for P-72's own sMCI vs pMCI result
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (P-72 baseline sMRI/FDG-PET pairs; P-3 ADNI1/ADNI2)
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal (P-72 subject-level hold-out averaged over three splits; P-3 5-fold CV)
gates.modality_family: partial: P-72's headline results fuse structural MRI with FDG-PET; P-3 is structural MRI only. P-72's sMRI-only branch matches P-3's modality

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as claimed (AD vs NC accuracy vs MCI-conversion accuracy); compatible when P-72's own conversion result is used (both accuracy, 3-year conversion horizon)
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither paper reaches 0.97 on the conversion task (P-72 77.19%, P-3 74.61%); P-72's 94.61% concerns AD vs NC and is not a near-ceiling small-sample result.
independence: Shared data source: both draw on ADNI, so the MCI cohorts overlap in part; different groups (Sichuan University; La Trobe/Monash), no shared authors.
grounds: The record's claim 'P-72: 94.61% AD on T2' misreads P-72: 94.61% is its AD vs NC accuracy, not an MCI conversion result.
P-72's own MCI conversion accuracies (77.19% multimodal, 73.68% sMRI-only) sit close to P-3's 74.61% on the same ADNI 3-year conversion task, so the two papers agree rather than disagree.

The residual differences are a few points between different architectures and inputs on different ADNI subsets, with no reported uncertainty that excludes the other value and no ordering claim in either paper that the other refutes.

evidence_quotes.quote: Especially in AD diagnosis achieved an average accuracy of 94.61 %, which provides a more feasible technology for diagnostic assessment of patients with AD.

In total, our dataset has 850 subjects including 215 AD, 246 NC (Normal Contral) and 389 MCI. We further divided the acquired MCI category into 151 pMCI (progressive MCI) and 238 sMCI (stable MCI), MCI subjects who developed AD within 3 years were labeled as pMCI
For the classification of sMCI vs. pMCI, the accuracy based on sMRI and PET was 73.68 % and 75.44 %, respectively.
The best accuracy was achieved in both prediction of AD vs. NC with 94.61 % and sMCI vs. pMCI with 77.19 % respectively
Experimental results on the ADNI dataset show that CAAT achieves accuracy of 74.61 for classifying between pMCI and sMCI using only whole 3D images of the brain and no other ancillary information.
The dataset consists of 298 sMCI and 295 pMCI participants retrieved from datasets ANDI1 and ADNI2. Each subject had one structural T1 weighted MRI scan taken at the baseline.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-72: 94.61% AD on T2' attaches P-72's AD vs NC accuracy to the MCI-conversion task; P-72's T2 accuracy is 77.19% (multimodal) or 73.68% (sMRI only).
gap_magnitude 0.2 is computed from the wrong P-72 figure; the like-for-like gap is about 0.026 (multimodal) or -0.009 (sMRI only).
modality_family 'structural_mri' is only half right for P-72, whose headline results fuse sMRI grey matter with FDG-PET.
The earlier note 'Metric type unclear: Unknown / Acc' is resolvable from the PDF: P-72 reports accuracy.
The bridging list cites dozens of papers (C-index, nomogram and other-task results) as 'comparable task/dataset family'; none is needed or apt for this pair.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in the two documents; a genuine disagreement would require an MCI-conversion estimate from one paper whose uncertainty excludes the other's on a comparable input, which neither provides.
